validated_results.title: Serum Retinol and Carotenoid Concentrations and Prostate Cancer Risk: Results from the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Prospective nested case-control study investigating the association between serum retinol concentrations and risk of prostate cancer in the PCPT placebo arm.

extraction.population: Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial (PCPT) placebo arm

sample_size.excerpt: First, the large sample size of this nested case-control study (975 cases/1009 frequency-matched controls in the placebo arm, 708 cases/743 frequency-matched controls in the finasteride arm) allowed investigation of associations with low- and high-grade prostate cancer risk, as well as additional subgroup analyses by supplement use and reason for biopsy. In addition, the PCPT protocol included annual standardized prostate cancer screening and biopsy recommendations, as well as an end-of-study biopsy recommendation on all cancer-free men, which reduced the potential for screening-related detection bias.
sample_size.location: Materials and Methods, Data collection and laboratory methods, paragraph 3; total_n derived from reported group counts 975 + 1009 = 1984

cases.excerpt: Men diagnosed with cancer before a post-randomization blood sample was collected were excluded (n=44 cases), as were men with insufficient serum (n=22 cases, 4 controls), men with missing laboratory values due to a labeling error (n=44 cases, 35 controls), and men missing 1 or more covariates (n=16 cases, 18 controls). The final sample size for the present analysis was 975 cases/1009 controls in the placebo arm, and 708 cases/743 controls in the finasteride arm, and the mean (SD) length of time between serum sample collection and diagnosis (for cases) was 2.3 (1.2) years.
cases.location: Materials and Methods, Data collection and laboratory methods, paragraph 3

effect_size.excerpt: Serum retinol concentrations were associated with increased risk of total prostate cancer [OR (95% CI) comparing the highest quartile of serum retinol to the lowest: 1.30 (1.00, 1.68)] and high-grade prostate cancer [OR (95% CI): 1.74 (1.14, 2.68)] in the placebo arm of the trial only.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Serum retinol concentrations were associated with increased risk of total prostate cancer [OR (95% CI) comparing the highest quartile of serum retinol to the lowest: 1.30 (1.00, 1.68)] and high-grade prostate cancer [OR (95% CI): 1.74 (1.14, 2.68)] in the placebo arm of the trial only.

p_value.location: Table 3, Retinol Placebo Total Prostate Cancer

comparison.excerpt: comparing the highest quartile of serum retinol to the lowest: 1.30 (1.00, 1.68)

design.excerpt: This case-control study nested in the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial evaluated associations of serum retinol and carotenoids with total, low- and high-grade prostate cancer risk

timing.excerpt: In this prospective analysis of serum retinol, carotenoids and prostate cancer risk, we found positive associations between serum retinol and total and high-grade prostate cancer

continent.excerpt: Between 1993 and 1997, across 221 study centers in the United States, 18,880 men were randomized to finasteride (5 mg/d) or placebo for 7 years.
continent.location: Materials and Methods, Study design and population, paragraph 1

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A hexane extract of serum was injected onto a C-18 Spherisorb ODS-2 HPLC column (3 μm, 3.0 × 125 mm, Waters PSS838528) using a Agilent 1100 LC system equipped with quaternary pump, electronic degasser, thermostatted column compartment (set at 25°C), automatic sampler, diode array detector and ChemStation software.
exposure_measurement.location: Materials and Methods, Data collection and laboratory methods, paragraph 4
